background.title: Myanmar civil war (2021–present)
background.description: Ongoing armed conflict in Southeast Asia
background.extract: The Myanmar civil war began following the military coup on 1 February 2021. The seizure of power triggered mass anti-coup demonstrations and a violent crackdown by the Tatmadaw, which significantly escalated the country's longstanding insurgencies.
background.license: Wikipedia text is available under CC BY-SA 4.0

headlines.title: Rakhine Civil Society Urges UN No-Fly Zone as Civilian Deaths Soar
headlines.excerpt: Humanitarian and civil network in western Myanmar demands international intervention after regime airstrikes claim 62 lives in September alone.

headlines.title: Big Brother Defends Myanmar Regime at UN, Chinese Aid Shortfall, and More
headlines.excerpt: Also this week, the Myanmar–China oil pipeline reached a new milestone, and Shan representatives protested against “Sinicization” along the border.

headlines.title: Myanmar Regime Hosts Russian Mining Billionaire After Approving Gold Ventures
headlines.excerpt: Meeting between Min Aung Hlaing and Areal CEO Vladislav Sviblov sparks speculation Moscow may be seeking a slice of Myanmar’s rare earth bounty.

headlines.title: ASEAN Envoy Ends Myanmar Trip With No Public Aung San Suu Kyi Meeting
headlines.excerpt: Despite repeated ASEAN requests for access, Philippine Foreign Secretary Lazaro ended her Myanmar visit without a confirmed meeting with Aung San Suu Kyi.

headlines.title: Cartoon Campaign Boosts Myanmar Regime’s Hydropower Dreams
headlines.excerpt: In trying to revive the controversial Myitsone Dam project, the military regime is resorting to the oldest propaganda tools in the book.

headlines.title: Myanmar’s illicit economy fuels escalating violence, with civilians bearing the brunt
headlines.excerpt: Myanmar’s human rights situation is “catastrophic”, the UN independent expert on the country warned at a press briefing Thursday, as the war spirals with no end in sight.

headlines.title: Myanmar Regime Begins Releasing Rakhine Deportees After Malaysia Pressure
headlines.excerpt: Over 400 ethnic residents from war-torn state faced weeks of interrogation in detention centers after being sent back ‘voluntarily’ from Malaysia.

headlines.title: Myanmar Navy Loses 3 More Ships as Arakan Army Tightens Sittwe Noose
headlines.excerpt: Regime counteroffensive crumbles as ethnic army reports gains in battle for regime’s final strongholds in Rakhine State.

headlines.title: Myanmar Regime Seizes Historic Nawnghio Mosque Over Rebel Links
headlines.excerpt: Regime officials are denying Nawnghkio’s Muslim community a place of worship as part of a vendetta against anyone they suspect of aiding Ta’ang rebels when they ruled the town.

headlines.title: Myanmar’s Aung San Suu Kyi ‘sounds strong’ but is isolated, son says
headlines.excerpt: Kim Aris tells the Guardian chance to speak with detained Nobel laureate was ‘public relations’ move from military leaders Myanmar’s former democratic leader Aung San Suu Kyi appears to be in good physical and mental health but is living in near-complete isolation, her son has…
